name: OX Quiz Widget
description: A mobile-friendly O/X quiz interface for educational apps that shows one question at a time with immediate answer feedback and progress tracking.

requirement.summary: Build an interactive O/X quiz widget in which users read one question at a time, choose O or X, see whether they were correct along with an explanation, track their progress, and retry the quiz after finishing.
details: Display the quiz questions one at a time from a question list
Provide O and X answer buttons for the user to choose from
After an answer is selected, show whether it was correct and display an explanation for the question
Disable further answer selection for the current question once an answer is submitted
Provide a way to advance to the next question after the feedback is shown
Show progress to the user, e.g. '3/10 questions completed', with a visual progress bar
Show a completion state when all questions are answered, including a summary of the score
Provide a retry feature that resets all state and restarts the quiz from the first question

Structure the UI into these components: QuizContainer (overall quiz layout), QuestionCard (current question display), AnswerButtons (O/X selection buttons), ProgressBar (progress display), and ResultDisplay (correct/incorrect feedback)
Manage state for the current question index, the user's answers, correctness of each answer, and quiz completion status
Use a responsive layout optimized for mobile and tablet screen sizes
Apply transition animations when moving between questions and when revealing feedback, using Tailwind transition/animation utilities
Support keyboard navigation: all interactive elements are focusable via Tab, activate with Enter/Space, and offer optional shortcut keys (e.g. O/X keys or left/right arrows) for answering

Provide accessibility features, including ARIA labels on O/X buttons, an aria-live region announcing correct/incorrect results, visible focus indicators, and progressbar semantics with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax
Use a color scheme of green for correct answers, red for incorrect answers, and gray for neutral or unselected states
Use the system default font stack
Include sample quiz data with about 10 questions, each with an id, question text, correct answer (O or X), and explanation
Type the question data and component props with TypeScript interfaces
